verifications.claim: El Niño conditions are expected to develop by summer 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'likely to develop this summer'; R2: 'likely emerge this summer'; R3: 'June-August 2026, El Niño is likely to emerge'; R4: 'develop this summer'; R5: 'May-July 2026, El Niño is likely'; R7: 'develop later in 2026 ... late summer'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly state El Niño expected in summer 2026 (June-August or overlapping periods).

verifications.claim: There is a 62% chance of El Niño emerging during June-August 2026 and persisting through the end of 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: '62% chance that El Niño will emerge between June and August ... persist through the rest of the year'; R3: 'June-August 2026, El Niño ... (62% chance) and persist through at least the end of 2026'; R7: '62% ... late summer ... persist through at least the end of 2026'
verifications.reasoning: Exact probability, period, and persistence directly stated in multiple sources.

verifications.claim: ENSO is currently in a neutral phase.
verifications.label: AMBIGUOUS
verifications.evidence: R3: 'La Niña continued in February 2026 ... transition to ENSO-neutral ... next month'; R4: 'La Niña conditions ... remain in place for now'; R5: 'ENSO-neutral conditions are present'; R6: '60% chance of ENSO neutral conditions ... March–May 2026'
verifications.reasoning: Sources contradict: earlier ones indicate ongoing La Niña or transition, later one (R5) states neutral present.

verifications.claim: A transition to El Niño is anticipated for the summer of 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'develop this summer'; R2: 'emerge this summer'; R3: 'transition to El Niño ... June-August 2026'; R4: 'shift ... this summer'; R5: 'transition to El Niño ... May-July 2026'; R7: 'El Niño forming in the late summer'
verifications.reasoning: Direct anticipation of transition to El Niño in summer 2026 across multiple sources.

verifications.claim: The likelihood of a transition to El Niño is increasing to around 40% by May-July 2026.
verifications.label: AMBIGUOUS
verifications.evidence: R5: 'May-July 2026, El Niño ... (61% chance)'; R6: 'chance of an El Niño increases steadily to around 40% ... May-July'; R3: 'ENSO-neutral ... through May-July 2026 (55% chance)'
verifications.reasoning: R6 supports ~40% exactly, but R5 states 61% and R3 implies lower via 55% neutral; contradictory probabilities.

verifications.claim: There is a 1-in-3 chance of a "strong" El Niño developing between October and December 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'one in three chance the next El Niño will be at least as strong as the last one'; R3: '1-in-3 chance that it would be "strong" during October-December 2026'; R7: '1-in-3 chance ... "strong" during October-December 2026'
verifications.reasoning: Exact phrasing and details directly match multiple sources.

verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: R1: 'pushed global temperatures ... above 1.5 degrees ... for the first time'; R2: 'long, strong El Niño ... helped shatter global temperature records'; R6: 'one of the five strongest on record'; R7: 'record-breaking ... temperature in 2024'
verifications.reasoning: Sources describe it as strong with record impacts/temps, but not explicitly the most record-setting El Niño itself (e.g., one of five strongest).
